definitionEn: the different parts, substances or people that something is made up of
senseNote: Выбрано значение «состав» (из чего что-то состоит); «сочинение» и «музыкальное произведение» — другие, более базовые значения.
situation: You describe which substances, parts or kinds of people something consists of, and in what proportions.

examples.text: Scientists analysed the [[composition]] of the rock samples to find out which minerals they contained.
The new board has a more balanced [[composition]], with equal numbers of men and women.
The [[composition]] of the class has changed: half the students now come from abroad.

texts: Experts studied the [[composition]] of the paint to date the old portrait.
The ethnic [[composition]] of the neighbourhood has changed a lot since the 1990s.
Any change to the [[composition]] of the committee needs a vote by all members.

badCollocation.noteRu: О еде и блюдах говорят ingredients: What are the ingredients? Composition звучит как химический анализ.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Из чего состоит вещество — chemical composition. Construction — строительство, compilation — сборник, arrangement — расположение или договорённость.

nuance.text: In terms of its [[composition]], air is roughly 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
nuance.explanationRu: Composition — из чего состоит вещество и в каких пропорциях. Structure — как части устроены и связаны; проценты газов — это состав, а не строение.

reverse.text: The steel [[structure]] of the bridge is designed to move slightly in strong winds.
reverse.explanationRu: Каркас, конструкция моста — structure. Composition говорит о веществах и пропорциях, а не о том, как собрана конструкция.

fixIt.text: The [[staff]] of the jury, nine men and three women, was criticised by the defence.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Состав» группы людей — composition (или makeup). Staff — сотрудники организации, у присяжных их нет.

wordFormation.text: Changes in the [[composition]] of the workforce mean that most employees are now over fifty.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "They've announced the new project team: six engineers and not a single designer."
options: Nice, I love that composition — the melody is really catchy.
That's a strange team composition for a project that's all about design.
The composition of the aforementioned team is hereby acknowledged as suboptimal.
reply.explanationRu: Composition здесь — состав команды. В первом ответе слово понято как музыкальное произведение, третий звучит канцелярски для рабочего чата.

definitionEn: to weaken something important, such as safety or quality, or put it at risk
senseNote: Выбрано значение «ставить под угрозу, подрывать» (compromise security); базовое «идти на компромисс» (B2) не отрабатывается.
situation: Careless actions or weak points make safety, security, quality or trust less reliable or put them in danger.

examples.text: Clicking on that link may have [[compromised]] your account, so change your password now.
Managers were warned that cutting staff training would [[compromise]] safety at the plant.
Accepting gifts from the companies they write about could [[compromise]] a journalist's independence.

texts: Months of treatment had left her immune system badly [[compromised]].
Investors fear the bank's reputation has been [[compromised]] by the scandal.
Police believe the witness's safety may already have been [[compromised]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Жизнь человека ставят под угрозу глаголами endanger или put at risk. Compromise — о безопасности, качестве, репутации, независимости.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Безопасность, качество, репутацию подрывают глаголом compromise. Spoil — испортить (вечер, еду), hurt и injure — ранить, причинить боль.

nuance.text: A single stolen laptop could [[compromise]] the security of the whole company.
nuance.explanationRu: Compromise — ослабить, поставить под угрозу (безопасность, качество). Violate — нарушить закон, правило или права; украденный ноутбук ничего не нарушает, он создаёт угрозу.

reverse.text: The factory was fined for [[violating]] health and safety regulations.
reverse.explanationRu: Правила и законы нарушают — violate. Compromise относится к самой безопасности или качеству, а не к правилам.

fixIt.text: One weak password can [[break]] the security of the entire network.
fixIt.explanationRu: Break security так не говорят: безопасность ставят под угрозу — compromise (или нарушают — breach).

reply.context: Your IT manager emails: "Someone logged into your work account from another country last night."
options: Great, so we've finally compromised on the new password rules?
Kindly be advised that my account is compromised henceforth.
Oh no, so my account has been compromised? I'll change my password right away.
reply.explanationRu: Compromised account — взломанный аккаунт, его безопасность под угрозой. В первом ответе слово понято как «договориться», второй звучит как нелепая канцелярская отписка.

rewrite.original: Poor maintenance has put the safety of the old bridge at risk.
rewrite.frame: The safety of the old bridge ____ by poor maintenance.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the safety has been compromised.

definitionEn: to calculate a figure or result, especially with a machine or a formula
situation: You work out an exact number or result, usually with software, a formula or large amounts of data.

examples.text: Using wind and temperature data, the model [[computes]] how far the smoke is likely to spread.
The app [[computes]] how much tax you owe from the receipts you upload.
In the exam you may use a calculator to [[compute]] the averages, but you must show your method.

texts: The final score is [[computed]] from the judges' marks and the public vote.
Your pension is [[computed]] on the basis of your last three years' salary.
The distance to the star was [[computed]] from measurements of its brightness.

badCollocation.noteRu: Людей и предметы просто считают — count the guests. Compute — вычислять результат по формуле или данным.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Среднее, вероятность, стоимость вычисляют — compute (или calculate). Count — пересчитывать предметы, solve — решать задачу, number — нумеровать.

nuance.text: Every night the system [[computes]] the average delivery time for each region.
nuance.explanationRu: Count — пересчитывать предметы по одному (count the boxes). Compute — вычислять результат по данным или формуле: среднее, вероятность, стоимость.

reverse.text: Can you [[count]] how many chairs we have in the hall?
reverse.explanationRu: Стулья в зале просто пересчитывают — count. Compute звучит так, будто нужна сложная формула.

fixIt.text: The forecasting software [[counts]] the probability of rain for every hour of the day.
fixIt.explanationRu: Вероятность не пересчитывают по одному, как предметы (count), а вычисляют — computes.

wordFormation.text: Modern weather forecasts depend on huge amounts of [[computation]].

definitionEn: to hide something or someone, or to keep a fact or feeling secret
situation: Someone deliberately keeps an object, a fact or an emotion out of sight so that others will not notice it.

examples.text: She [[concealed]] the letter inside a book so that her flatmates wouldn't find it.
The director was accused of [[concealing]] important evidence from the police.
He laughed at the joke to [[conceal]] the fact that he hadn't understood it.

texts: Good make-up can [[conceal]] the signs of a sleepless night.
The report was written to [[conceal]] the real cost of the project.
He turned away to [[conceal]] the tears in his eyes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Секрет хранят — keep a secret. Conceal — скрывать факты, чувства, улики: conceal the truth.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Скрывать правду от кого-то — conceal (или hide) the truth from someone. Close и lock — закрывать дверь или замок, save — спасать или копить.

nuance.text: The old house has a narrow staircase [[concealed]] behind a bookcase.
nuance.explanationRu: Conceal — спрятать так, чтобы не было видно (за шкафом). Disguise — замаскировать под что-то другое: a door disguised as a bookcase. С behind подходит только conceal.

reverse.text: He [[disguised]] his voice so the caller wouldn't recognise him.
reverse.explanationRu: Голос не прячут, а меняют, чтобы не узнали, — disguise. Conceal значит убрать с глаз или скрыть факт.

fixIt.text: For months the manager [[covered]] the real sales figures from the rest of the team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cover — накрыть сверху. Скрыть информацию от кого-то — conceal something from someone (или cover up).

wordFormation.text: The [[concealment]] of the test results led to a public inquiry.

reply.context: In a meeting, your boss asks: "Why didn't the client hear about the delay from us?"
options: We concealed the delay to them in detail in yesterday's email.
We never meant to conceal it — we only found out about the delay this morning.
It was never our intention to conceal the aforementioned delay from the esteemed client.
reply.explanationRu: Conceal — скрывать информацию, второй ответ естественный. В первом conceal ошибочно значит «сообщить», третий звучит напыщенно для обычного разговора.

definitionEn: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true or that you were wrong
senseNote: Выбрано значение «неохотно признать правоту»; значения «пропустить гол» и «уступить (территорию, право)» не отрабатываются.
situation: After arguing or resisting for some time, you finally admit that the other person has a point.

examples.text: After weeks of criticism, the minister finally [[conceded]] that the new rules had been introduced too quickly.
Afterwards, the coach honestly [[conceded]] that his team had been lucky to win.
"Fine, you might be right," she [[conceded]], still looking annoyed.

texts: Even his critics [[concede]] that he is a brilliant negotiator.
I [[concede]] that my first draft was far too long.
Most scientists now [[concede]] that the early data was misleading.

badCollocation.noteRu: Concede не употребляется с with: говорят concede that или concede a point, а «согласиться с кем-то» — agree with someone.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Признать поражение — concede defeat (или admit, accept defeat). Agree требует with или to, allow — разрешать, grant — предоставлять.

nuance.text: In the final debate, the candidate [[conceded]] that her opponent had made a fair point.
nuance.explanationRu: Concede — признать правоту оппонента в споре. Confess — сознаться в чём-то плохом или постыдном; признать чужой хороший аргумент не стыдно, поэтому confess звучит странно.

reverse.text: After hours of questioning, he [[confessed]] to the robbery.
reverse.explanationRu: Сознаться в преступлении — confess to a crime. Concede — признать правоту или поражение; «concede to the robbery» не говорят.

fixIt.text: After a long argument, my brother finally [[gave in]] that I had been right all along.
fixIt.explanationRu: Give in — сдаться, уступить; после него не ставят that. Признать, что кто-то прав, — concede that.

reply.context: During debate practice, your opponent says: "You have to admit my figures are more recent than yours."
options: Fair enough, I'll concede that point, but my main argument still stands.
No way, I concede your figures completely — they're simply wrong.
I hereby formally concede, pursuant to the aforementioned statistical data.
reply.explanationRu: Concede a point — признать правоту в одном вопросе. Во втором ответе concede ошибочно значит «отвергать», третий звучит как юридический документ.

rewrite.original: Although he didn't want to, Tom admitted that his sister was right.
rewrite.explanationRu: Reluctantly concede that — неохотно признать, что кто-то прав.

definitionEn: to form an idea or plan in your mind, or to imagine something
senseNote: Выбрано значение «задумать, представить себе»; значение «зачать ребёнка» не отрабатывается.
situation: Someone comes up with an original plan in their head, or manages to picture something in their mind.

examples.text: The festival was [[conceived]] by two students who wanted to bring live music to their town.
I can't [[conceive]] of a better way to spend a Sunday than walking in the hills.
Ten years ago, nobody could have [[conceived]] that the small start-up would become a global company.

texts: The bridge was [[conceived]] as a symbol of the city's new confidence.
The novel was [[conceived]] during a long train journey across Canada.
The project was badly [[conceived]] and ran out of money within a year.

badCollocation.noteRu: После conceive не ставят about: говорят conceive of something или conceive a plan, а «думать о проблеме» — think about a problem.

collocationTask.prompt: It's hard to ___ of a world without music.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Conceive of something — представить себе что-то. После imagine, invent и suppose предлог of не ставят: imagine a world.

nuance.text: Two engineers [[conceived]] the plan for a floating solar farm on the old reservoir.
nuance.explanationRu: Conceive a plan — придумать и продумать план или проект. Imagine — представить картинку в голове, часто нереальную; «imagine a plan» звучит странно.

reverse.text: Close your eyes and [[imagine]] you're lying on a warm beach.
reverse.explanationRu: Представить себе картинку — imagine. Conceive — книжное слово про идеи и планы, в такой просьбе не подходит.

fixIt.text: She first [[invented]] the plan for the charity while she was working as a nurse abroad.
fixIt.explanationRu: Invent — изобрести устройство или способ. План или проект задумывают — conceive a plan.

wordFormation.text: It is [[conceivable]] that prices will fall again next year, though few experts expect it.

rewrite.original: It was impossible for me to imagine life without my children.
rewrite.frame: I couldn't ____ life without my children.
rewrite.explanationRu: Conceive of something — представить себе что-то (книжно).

definitionEn: an idea or understanding of what something is like or should be
senseNote: Выбрано значение «представление, понимание» (a conception of justice); значение «зачатие» не отрабатывается.
situation: You describe how a person, group or culture understands what something is, means or ought to be.

examples.text: Young children have a very different [[conception]] of time: for them, a week can feel endless.
Our [[conception]] of what counts as a family has changed a great deal over the last fifty years.
The new manager's [[conception]] of teamwork seemed to mean everyone simply agreeing with her.

texts: Each generation has its own [[conception]] of success.
Her [[conception]] of a relaxing holiday involves climbing three mountains.
The film questions our [[conception]] of what makes a hero.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Концепция» продукта или бренда — concept: a marketing concept. Conception — чьё-то представление о чём-то.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Узкое представление об успехе — a narrow conception of success. Conceit — самомнение, concession — уступка, conscience — совесть.

nuance.text: The study challenges the popular [[conception]] of teenagers as lazy and selfish.
nuance.explanationRu: Conception — представление людей о ком-то или чём-то (the popular conception of teenagers). Concept — сама идея или замысел (a new café concept); здесь речь о взглядах.

reverse.text: The restaurant's [[concept]] is simple: you pay only for the time you spend there.
reverse.explanationRu: Замысел, «концепция» бизнеса или продукта — concept. Conception — чьё-то представление о чём-то, к ресторану не подходит.

fixIt.text: Medieval maps show that people then had a very limited [[presentation]] of how big the world was.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Представление о чём-то» — conception (или idea), а не presentation: presentation — это доклад или показ.

wordFormation.text: Our [[conception]] of privacy has changed since everyone started carrying a smartphone.

rewrite.original: People today understand childhood very differently from people in the past.
rewrite.frame: Our ____ childhood is very different from that of people in the past.
rewrite.explanationRu: A conception of something — представление о чём-то.

definitionEn: something that you agree to give up or allow in order to reach an agreement
senseNote: Выбрано значение «уступка» (make concessions); значения «льготная скидка» и «право на торговлю» не отрабатываются.
situation: During a negotiation or dispute, one side gives up part of what it wanted so that both sides can agree.

examples.text: After a week of strikes, management made several [[concessions]], including shorter shifts and a pay rise.
Letting my sister choose where we went on holiday was a big [[concession]] on my part.
In the trade talks, neither country was willing to offer [[concessions]] on farming.

texts: Working from home on Fridays was a small [[concession]], but staff appreciated it.
The new law was widely seen as a [[concession]] to farmers.
Watching her favourite film again was my only [[concession]] all weekend.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Пойти на уступки» — make concessions; калька go on concessions неверна.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Идти на уступки — make concessions. Do, take и put с concession не сочетаются.

nuance.text: As a [[concession]] to local residents, the airport will stop night flights.
nuance.explanationRu: Concession — то, что одна сторона уступает другой (a concession to residents). Compromise — договорённость, где уступают обе стороны; «a compromise to someone» не говорят.

reverse.text: After hours of arguing, the two partners finally reached a [[compromise]].
reverse.explanationRu: Прийти к компромиссу — reach a compromise: уступают обе стороны. Concession делают (make), а не «достигают».

fixIt.text: To end the strike, the government made an important [[compromise]] to nurses on pay.
fixIt.explanationRu: Compromise — взаимное соглашение. То, что одна сторона даёт другой, — concession: make a concession to someone.

wordFormation.text: Every [[concession]] we made seemed to encourage the other side to demand more.

reply.context: Your flatmate says: "OK, you can have the bigger room, but then you pay a bit more rent."
options: Thanks, but I don't need a concession — I'm not a student any more.
Your concession is hereby accepted; the relevant documentation will follow.
That's quite a concession — thanks! I'm happy to pay a bit extra.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь concession — уступка соседа по квартире. В первом ответе слово понято как льготная скидка для студентов, второй звучит как официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: Neither side was willing to give up anything to reach an agreement.

definitionEn: to say publicly and strongly that something or someone is morally wrong
senseNote: Выбрано значение «публично осуждать»; значения «приговаривать (к наказанию)» и «признавать здание непригодным» не отрабатываются.
situation: Leaders, groups or organisations publicly declare that an action or statement is completely unacceptable.

examples.text: Several charities [[condemned]] the decision to cut funding for mental health services.
The company quickly [[condemned]] the manager's comments and said they did not reflect its values.
Many people [[condemn]] fast fashion, but they still buy cheap clothes every season.

texts: The attack was [[condemned]] by religious leaders of every faith.
His remarks were widely [[condemned]] as offensive and out of date.
Testing cosmetics on animals has long been [[condemned]] by many scientists.

badCollocation.noteRu: Condemn — резкое публичное осуждение серьёзных поступков. За опоздание друга можно разве что criticise или tell off.

collocationTask.prompt: The decision was widely ___ by teachers.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Решение или поступок «широко осуждают» — widely condemned. Blame и accuse говорят о людях (blame someone for), judge — оценивать или судить.

nuance.text: The football club [[condemned]] the fans' behaviour and promised to ban those responsible.
nuance.explanationRu: Condemn — публично осудить поступок как недопустимый. Blame — считать кого-то виноватым в чём-то: blame someone for something; без for фраза не работает.

reverse.text: Don't [[blame]] yourself: the accident wasn't your fault.
reverse.explanationRu: Винить себя — blame yourself. Condemn — публичное моральное осуждение, для утешения друга слишком резко.

fixIt.text: Human rights groups sharply [[judged]] the arrest of the two journalists.
fixIt.explanationRu: Публично и резко «осудить» — condemn. Judge — оценивать или судить, со sharply так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: The plan to close the library drew strong [[condemnation]] from parents and teachers.

reply.context: A friend texts: "The mayor called the vandalism in the park 'completely unacceptable'."
options: Good. It's right that she condemned it so clearly.
Really? Why would she condemn the park? It's lovely.
One must concur that the mayor's condemnation was wholly appropriate.
reply.explanationRu: Condemn — публично осудить поступок: мэр осудила вандализм. Во втором ответе слово отнесено к самому парку, третий звучит слишком книжно для переписки с другом.

rewrite.original: Environmental groups strongly criticised the plan, calling it dangerous.
rewrite.explanationRu: Condemn something as dangerous — осудить что-то, назвав опасным.

definitionEn: to train someone over time to behave, think or react in a particular way
senseNote: Выбрано значение «приучать, формировать поведение» (be conditioned to do something); значение «ухаживать (за волосами)» не отрабатывается.
situation: Repeated experience, training or advertising makes people or animals automatically behave or think in a certain way.

examples.text: In the experiment, the dogs were [[conditioned]] to expect food whenever they heard a bell.
We have been [[conditioned]] by advertising to believe that newer always means better.
Years of early shifts have [[conditioned]] her to wake up at five, even on holiday.

texts: Many of us are [[conditioned]] to check our phones the moment we wake up.
Soldiers are [[conditioned]] to obey orders without questioning them.
Girls were once [[conditioned]] to believe that science was not for them.

badCollocation.noteRu: Привычку вырабатывают — develop или form a habit. Condition относится к людям и животным: condition someone to do something.

collocationTask.prompt: We are ___ to believe that being busy means being successful.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be conditioned to do something — быть приученным к чему-то, часто незаметно. После be used to нужен -ing, adapted — приспособленный, addicted — зависимый.

nuance.text: Years of strict schooling had [[conditioned]] him to raise his hand before speaking.
nuance.explanationRu: Condition — незаметно «запрограммировать» поведение (школа, опыт, реклама). Accustom — приучить к условиям: accustomed to the noise; с to raise не сочетается.

reverse.text: After a month in Norway, we had become [[accustomed]] to the long summer evenings.
reverse.explanationRu: Привыкнуть к обстановке — become accustomed to. Condition — выработать реакцию или поведение, к летним вечерам не подходит.

fixIt.text: Most of us have been [[adjusted]] to see a suntan as a sign of good health.
fixIt.explanationRu: Adjust — настраивать или приспосабливаться. «Нас приучили так думать» — we have been conditioned to see или think.

wordFormation.text: Social [[conditioning]] teaches many boys to hide their feelings.

reply.context: A friend says: "I feel guilty whenever I take a day off, even when I'm ill."
options: Maybe your flat needs conditioning — it's far too hot in there.
It would appear that you have undergone a process of behavioural conditioning.
I think we've been conditioned to see rest as laziness. It isn't.
reply.explanationRu: Be conditioned to — быть «приученным» что-то чувствовать или думать. Первый ответ путает с кондиционером, второй звучит как научная статья, а не разговор с другом.
